About me

After being born and raised in northern Alberta, I chose to attend the University of British Columbia Okanagan in Kelowna, BC to pursue a career in Mechanical Engineering.

During my undergraduate studies I was able to develop my engineering skills by being a part of the UBCO Motorsports as well as complete a variety of industry placements and international experiences.

These experiences complimented my studies, and I graduated with a Bachelors of Applied Science in Mechanical Engineering with distinction and completed the Co-operative Education Program.

Wanting to expand my engineering knowledge, I pursued my Masters of Applied Science in Mechanical and Mechatronics Engineering at the University of Waterloo where I specialized in Materials Engineering and Processing.

My research spans laser cladding of nickel superalloys, alloy design for recycled aluminum, and metal additive manufacturing. I have collaborated with industry partners such as Teck Resources and Canmet MATERIALS, and was a visiting scientist at the Technical University of Munich.

Designed, prototyped, iterated, and tested a benchmark for metal additive manufacturing, 3DCastleBenchy.

Read more

The deceptively simple design contains at least 24 metrics for evaluating dimensional accuracy for conformal cooling channels, overhangs and arches, capturing the imagination of the user through its aesthetics.

The CAD files are freely available with the related publication, 3DCastleBenchy: a process-independent benchmark for additive manufacturing.

2024 – 2026
AluminumRecycling

Laser remelting of recycled Al6061

University of Waterloo · MASc research
Best Paper MetSoc Light Metals2 publications

Investigated aluminum 6061 containing iron and zinc impurities as a feedstock for AM, to encourage recyclability and circular economy.

Read more

I analyzed dozens of laser remelted samples with varying impurity levels, laser power and speed. Iron had an overall beneficial effect and could reduce or nearly eliminate crack susceptibility. Zn had minimal effect, so compositional tolerances could be loosened when recycling Al6061 for AM feedstock, contradicting existing industry practice.

I was awarded the MetSoc Light Metals Best Paper Award after presenting at the 2025 Conference of Metallurgists (COM).
